impact.outsideBody: Damage, critical facilities, cell network, emergency routes, district arrivals and the tsunami are modelled only for the Marmara region. Here the simulation shows the wavefronts, ground motion and intensity, with site conditions from the USGS global Vs30 model.
impact.title: Arrival by district

telemetry.method: Stochastic method (Boore 2003), scaled to the ASB14 median
telemetry.scaleNote: Each trace is scaled to its own peak.
telemetry.observedMethod: Acceleration record from the KOERI EIDA node; counts converted to cm/s² with the instrument sensitivity after removing the pre-event mean.

eew.title: Early warning (simulated)
eew.waiting: Location and magnitude are estimated once four stations have triggered and recorded 3 s of P wave.
eew.unavailable: Fewer than four stations triggered, so no early warning was issued.
eew.note: Magnitude from Pd in the first 3 s of P; large events are underestimated, as in real systems. Data transmission and processing delays are not modelled.

damage.title: Damage and losses (simulated, night)
damage.note: Expected values from the GEM 2025 vulnerability model for Türkiye over the ground-motion uncertainty, residents at home (03:00). Building stock outside İstanbul is estimated. Not definitive damage information.

infra.title: Critical facilities
infra.note: Hospitals, fire stations and police (OpenStreetMap), assessed with one reinforced-concrete class; the state thresholds (5 % and 20 % expected loss) are a display assumption.

network.title: Cell network (simulation)
network.syntheticSites: Sites are synthetic, placed from population with ITU-R M.2135 spacing.
network.note: Demand up to 55× the busy hour (2011 Tōhoku), for those who felt the shaking, decaying over about 1.4 h; host-building damage from the facility class. Power cuts are not modelled.

routing.title: Emergency response (simulation)
routing.cutOff_one: {{count}} district cannot be reached by road
routing.cutOff_other: {{count}} districts cannot be reached by road
routing.note: Shortest routes on OpenStreetMap major roads at legal speed limits, from fire stations and to hospitals still in service. Bridges close from Hazus fragility; narrow urban streets slow with expected building loss (assumption).

tsunami.title: Tsunami (simulation, educational)
tsunami.computing: Computing the wave over the Marmara Sea…
tsunami.error: The tsunami could not be computed.
tsunami.note: Okada (1985) seafloor motion of the rupture, linear shallow-water waves on EMODnet bathymetry (500 m). No run-up, no landslide sources; heights are offshore estimates near the coast.

aftershocks.title: Aftershocks (simulation)
aftershocks.note: A synthetic sequence from the Reasenberg & Jones (1989) generic California model (modified Omori decay, Gutenberg–Richter magnitudes); locations scattered along the rupture. Probabilities come from the same model, not an official forecast.

replay.note: Replays use the catalog magnitude and hypocentre: within 15 km of a fault the rupture is placed on it, otherwise at the epicentre along the nearest fault's strike. Where KOERI recorded strong motion, telemetry shows the real record instead of the synthetic one.

live.empty: No earthquakes in this scope in the last 7 days.
live.simulateHint: Simulate this earthquake with its catalog magnitude and hypocentre.
live.note: The last 7 days of earthquakes in Türkiye from AFAD, Kandilli (KOERI) and EMSC, and worldwide (M 4.5 and above) from USGS; reports within 30 s and 30 km are merged, with values taken first from the national agency. Refreshed every minute. Not an official warning system.

methods.shaking: Finite-fault rupture (Wells and Coppersmith 1994), IASP91 travel times, Akkar-Sandıkkaya-Bommer (2014) median ground motion with the USGS Vs30 site term, Worden et al. (2012) intensity conversion. Fault geometry from EFSM20.

about.title: About quakeTrace
about.description: An in-browser earthquake simulation and real-time monitoring screen for the Marmara region.

overview.disclaimerTitle: A simulation, not an official warning system
overview.disclaimer: Scenarios are model estimates, not real earthquake warnings, damage assessments or forecasts. For official information follow AFAD and the Kandilli Observatory. Real data (live earthquakes, observed records) is always labelled with its source.
overview.what: Start a rupture on a fault and watch P and S waves spread across the districts second by second, with station records, early warning, damage, network and response status, tsunami and aftershocks on one timeline. All physics runs in the browser; no server or account is needed.

modes.presets: Presets: expected-earthquake scenarios on the Main Marmara Fault.
modes.editor: Editor: your own scenario on any mapped fault, with magnitude, hypocentre, depth and seed.
modes.replay: Historical: the 1999, 2019 and 2025 earthquakes with USGS parameters; real acceleration records where KOERI stations recorded them.
modes.live: Live: the last 7 days of earthquakes from the AFAD, Kandilli, EMSC and USGS catalogs; M 4 and above can be simulated.

overview.share: The address bar always holds the running scenario; anyone with the link sees the same result. The Events panel exports a report (PDF), GeoJSON and CSV.

methods.intro: Every model rests on a published source; coefficients are tested against reference implementations. The values below are median (expected) estimates.

rupture.title: Rupture
rupture.body: Planar finite fault below the fault trace; magnitude and rupture area from Wells and Coppersmith (1994). The rupture front spreads from the hypocentre at 0.8 Vs (Heaton, 1990). Fault geometry from EFSM20 (Basili et al., 2024).

waves.title: Wave arrivals
waves.body: First arrivals of direct and refracted waves in the IASP91 crust (Kennett and Engdahl, 1991), with the rupture time of each subfault added.

groundMotion.title: Ground motion and intensity
groundMotion.body: Akkar, Sandıkkaya and Bommer (2014) PGA, PGV and spectral acceleration with the USGS Vs30 site term. Intensity (MMI) from Worden et al. (2012).

records.title: Station records
records.body: Three-component synthetic accelerograms from the Boore (2003) stochastic method, scaled to the ASB14 median so they agree with the map. Triggers by STA/LTA (Trnkoczy, 2012).

eew.title: Early warning
eew.body: Location by grid search on the first four stations; magnitude from Pd in the first 3 s of P (Wu and Zhao, 2006). No transmission or processing delays.

damage.title: Damage and losses
damage.body: GEM 2025 vulnerability functions for Türkiye, expected values over the ground-motion uncertainty; night scenario. District ranking compared with the İBB 2019 scenario.

network.title: Cell network
network.body: Synthetic cell sites at ITU-R M.2135 spacings by population; call demand after the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake (NTT DOCOMO) and its decay (Bagrow et al., 2011).

routing.title: Emergency response
routing.body: OpenStreetMap major roads at legal speed limits; bridges by Hazus fragility, streets slowed by expected building loss (assumption). Shortest routes from fire stations and to hospitals.

tsunami.title: Tsunami
tsunami.body: Okada (1985) seafloor displacement and linear shallow-water waves on EMODnet bathymetry. No run-up or landslide sources; educational.

aftershocks.title: Aftershocks
aftershocks.body: A synthetic 72-hour sequence and 24-hour probabilities from the Reasenberg and Jones (1989) generic California parameters.

methods.validation: Model PGA was compared with values observed at KOERI strong-motion stations (geometric mean of the horizontals). Mean ln residual ln(observed/model): +0.10 at 12 stations for the 2019 Silivri Mw 5.7 earthquake, +0.09 at 43 stations for the 2025 Marmara Ereğlisi Mw 6.2 earthquake; station-to-station scatter about 0.5. Target ±0.3.
methods.limits: All results are medians; uncertainty bands are not shown. Building stock outside İstanbul is estimated. Power cuts, traffic and ferries are not modelled. Aftershock parameters are not fitted to the Marmara region.
